name: Criticism
overview: Scripture teaches that criticism must be approached with humility, grace, and self-examination. Believers are warned against judging others harshly, as doing so invites judgment upon themselves (Matthew 7:1). When addressing a brother's fault, restoration should be done gently and with meekness, mindful of one's own vulnerability to temptation (Galatians 6:1). Communication should build up rather than tear down, avoiding corrupt or harmful speech and instead ministering grace to others (Ephesians 4:29). Additionally, Christians are encouraged to be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger (James 1:19), refraining from speaking evil or judging one another in a way that usurps God's law (James 4:11).
